quote.translation: Because the purpose acts as a cause and produces the means as its result, what was originally result becomes cause, and what was originally cause becomes result.

quote.translation: Renouvier says accordingly that "the means is a kind of result peculiar to the cause called teleological" (Renouvier, Traité de Logique générale, 1912, II, p. 164), and so, to borrow the words of Hamelin, purposiveness is "determination by the future" (Hamelin, Essai sur les éléments principaux de la représentation, 2e éd., p. 332).
The future ought to lack actuality, and it can take on actuality and act as a cause only through the fact of the temporal anticipation of consciousness.

regions.text: さうして、現實性を鉄いてるる筈の未来が、現實性を機びて原因として働くことが出來るのは、意識の時間的先取の事

quote.translation: Purposiveness is consequently, in the strict sense, a concept whose validity is confined to the range of consciousness.

regions.text: によるのほかはないから、目性といふことは厳密には意識の範園に限り妥當性をもつた概念である。この機念を意識の範囲を超えて自然界にも構成的原理として認めようとするには恐らくべルグッンの謂はゆる「取消された意識』（conscienceamnulee）（Bergson,LEvolutionc

quote.translation: If we wish to acknowledge this concept as a constitutive principle in the natural world too, beyond the range of consciousness, there is probably no way of doing so except through the mediation of a concept of the unconscious understood as what Bergson calls "annulled consciousness" (conscience annulée) (Bergson, L'Évolution créatrice, 25 éd., p. 156).

regions.text: eatrice,25cd,p156）としての無意識の概念の媒介によるほかはないであらう。意識的行為が習慣によつて無意識的な反射運動に變ずる事實に基いて、意識が習慣によつて無意識になつた極限を自然界と見る考へ方がある。

quote.translation: There is a way of thinking that starts from the fact that conscious acts are changed by habit into unconscious reflex movements, and that sees the natural world as the limit at which consciousness has become unconscious through habit.

regions.text: 習慣とは謂はば意志が自然に至る微分的連穫である。

quote.translation: Habit is, so to speak, the differential continuity by which will passes over into nature.

regions.text: 「習慣の懸史は自由が自然へ踏還する路を表はす。成は寧ろ自然的自發性によつて自由の傾域が使されることを表はす』「かくして

quote.translation: "The history of habit represents the return of freedom to nature, or rather the invasion of the domain of freedom by natural spontaneity," and "thus perhaps the rule of knowledge and foresight appears in the domain of nature," as Ravaisson says (Ravaisson, De l'habitude, nouvelle éd. 1927, p. 62, 16).
